content.statement: Article 14 permits reasonable classification but forbids class legislation. A valid classification requires an intelligible differentia and a rational nexus between that differentia and the object of the law.
elements: Intelligible differentia distinguishing those grouped together from others left out
Rational relation between the differentia and the object sought to be achieved
content.development: Settled Article 14 doctrine in Indian constitutional law; modern overlay treats arbitrariness as inconsistent with equality.
content.application: Plead the class, object, differentia, and nexus; then test arbitrariness in operation.
exceptions: Special provisions expressly authorised by later clauses of Articles 15 and 16 are enabling clauses, not freestanding exceptions to invent
